$comment: Commands are opt-in and skills are opt-in. A hook fires whether or not
anybody remembered it, which is what makes it the mechanism that produces
A hook is not a control. It only fires inside the authoring tool; a
terminal in the same container has none. The authority is server-side —
branch protection, required checks, CODEOWNERS, the merge queue. The hooks
exist to fail fast and to teach; the branch rules exist to be true. Both
are needed, and there is one gate binary so the two can never disagree
The deny rules are the same idea, one step earlier: what nobody edits by hand
(the design's files, what a command generates, the recorded answers) and
what an assistant never does (force a push, push to a branch a pull request
owns). The reads denied are build output and data, which cost a session
